zh.sample:
# 写作与日常记录

一份清晰的文档，从标题下面的第一段正文开始。这份样张把日常笔记、项目记录和阅读摘录放在一起，你可以比较**重点文字**、*补充说明*、~~过期内容~~、==值得记住的句子==、`行内代码`和[参考链接](https://example.com)在同一段里的表现。

清晨打开笔记，先写下今天最想完成的一件事。有时只需要几句话，有时则要把背景、过程和结论慢慢展开。文字会随着预览宽度自然换行；段内的行距决定阅读是否紧凑，而段落之间的留白帮助读者停顿。调整主题时，可以观察这段较长的正文，看看字体、颜色和行距是否适合长时间阅读。

## 项目进展

这一周，我们把零散的想法整理成了可以讨论的初稿。比起急着写下结论，先把问题描述清楚，往往更容易找到下一步。

> 好的记录不需要面面俱到，但应该让未来的自己明白，当时为什么作出这个决定。

### 本周要做的事

任务列表适合快速浏览，正文则用来补充背景和约束。它们放在同一篇文档里，应当有清楚的层次，也保留相近的阅读节奏。

- 整理访谈记录，把相似的问题放在一起
- 完成第一版草稿，并收集同事的反馈
  - 确认标题、段落与表格的阅读顺序
- [x] 建立共享文档
- [ ] 安排下一次讨论

#### 观察与数据

下面的表格记录了几个阶段的进展。中文、English 和数字混排时，也应当容易辨认。

| 阶段 | 状态 | 记录数 |
| --- | --- | ---: |
| Research | 已完成 | 12 |
| Draft | 进行中 | 8 |
| Review | 待安排 | 3 |

##### 实现片段

代码块有独立的字体和配色，注释解释意图，关键字与字符串帮助读者快速找到信息。

```js
// 为每一份记录保留清晰的标题
function createNote(title) {
  const note = { title, version: 1 }
  return note
}
```

###### 后续安排

小标题下面也需要普通正文。下次打开这份记录时，可以从这里继续补充发现，而不用重新回忆整个过程。

en.sample:
# Writing and everyday notes

A clear document begins with the paragraph beneath its title. This sample brings together daily notes, project updates, and reading excerpts so you can compare **key points**, *extra context*, ~~outdated ideas~~, ==memorable sentences==, `inline code`, and [reference links](https://example.com) within real prose.

When you open your notebook in the morning, start with the one thing you want to finish today. A short thought may take only a sentence; a useful explanation often needs room for its background, process, and conclusion. This longer paragraph wraps naturally with the preview width. Line height shapes the rhythm within it, while the space between paragraphs gives readers a pause. Use it to judge whether the font, colors, and spacing feel comfortable for sustained reading.

## Project progress

This week, we turned scattered ideas into a draft that others can discuss. Describing the problem clearly helped us decide what to do next.

> A useful record does not need every detail. It should help your future self understand why a decision was made.

### This week's tasks

Lists make tasks easy to scan. The paragraphs around them explain the context and constraints, keeping the whole document connected.

- Group related questions from the interviews
- Finish the first draft and gather feedback
  - Check the order of headings, paragraphs, and tables
- [x] Create the shared document
- [ ] Schedule the next discussion

#### Observations and data

The table below tracks progress through a few stages. Words, 中文, and numbers should remain easy to distinguish when they appear together.

| Stage | Status | Records |
| --- | --- | ---: |
| Research | Complete | 12 |
| Draft | In progress | 8 |
| Review | Planned | 3 |

##### Implementation notes

Code has its own typeface and palette. Comments explain intent, while keywords and strings help readers find the relevant details.

```js
// Give every record a clear title
function createNote(title) {
  const note = { title, version: 1 }
  return note
}
```

###### Next steps

Even a small heading needs ordinary prose beneath it. When you return to these notes, continue from here without reconstructing the whole conversation.
